samples.summary: Pagination-bound test's comment claims a boundary the assertions never check (and that the code refuses)
samples.evidence: `gate 1b enumerates EVERY page...` says "Exactly 1000 files is fine; 10 full pages is what the bound allows, and an off-by-one here would refuse a legal PR" — but the only assertion built from `tenFullPages` (10 × 100 = exactly 1000 files) is `assert.equal(atTheBound.code, 1, ...)`, i.e. a refusal. `ciDefiningPathsChanged` loops `page <= 10` and only returns early on a SHORT page, so a PR with exactly 1000 files falls out of the loop and throws. No test asserts the accepting side of the bound (e.g. 9 full pages + a short 10th, or 999 files), so the off-by-one the comment claims to protect is uncovered and the comment gives false assurance about which side of the bound is legal.

samples.summary: set-state's rewritten CI-run read has no behavioral test — only a source-string grep
samples.evidence: `gatherSignals` now queries `/actions/workflows/${CI_WORKFLOW_FILE}/runs` and normalises through `ciConclusion` (so 'cancelled'/'timed_out' now become 'failure', and run selection changed from newest-by-created_at-and-name to newest-by-id). `gatherSignals` is not exported and scripts/agent/set-state.test.mjs contains no `spawnSync`/stub-`gh` process test (grep for STUB_GH/spawnSync in that file returns nothing) — it only unit-tests the pure helpers (`deriveState`, `computeLabelSet`, …). The only thing pinning the new reader is the string assertion in checks.test.mjs (`actions/workflows/${CI_WORKFLOW_FILE}/runs?head_sha=`), which cannot fail if the selection or the null/failure mapping regresses. Impact is contained (deriveState only tests `=== 'success'`, and reconcile is an advisory label), which is why this is minor rather than major.
searchedFor: read scripts/agent/checks.test.mjs 'the CI readers scope by workflow FILE' test

samples.summary: No test that gate 1 fails closed when the (newly rewritten) workflow-runs query errors
samples.evidence: `ciPassed` wraps the new scoped `gh api .../actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs` call in `try { … } catch { return false; }`. mark-ready.test.mjs's stub supports forcing failures via `cfg.fail`, and it is used for `pr view`, `pulls/7/files`, `pr ready`, `api -X PUT` and `pr comment` — but never for the workflow-runs endpoint. So the fail-closed behaviour of the one gate that means "the tests passed" is unasserted: a regression that returned `true` (or let the exception escape into a different exit code) on an unreadable Actions API would keep every test in the file green.
searchedFor: read all gate-1 tests in mark-ready.test.mjs

samples.summary: Inline-mirror equivalence fixtures never include a run without an `id`, the one input where the two copies differ
samples.evidence: checks.mjs `newestRun` compares `(r.id ?? 0) > (newest.id ?? 0)`; the extracted YAML mirror is `completed.reduce((n, r) => (n === null || r.id > n.id ? r : n), null)`. With a missing/undefined `id`, `r.id > n.id` is NaN-false while `(r.id ?? 0) > …` is defined — the copies can disagree. Every fixture in the `agent-rerun / agent-loop mirror ciRunToRerun inline` test constructs runs via `run(id, status, conclusion)` with a numeric id, so the equivalence claim ("the copies agree") is only demonstrated on the inputs where they cannot diverge.
searchedFor: read the mirror test fixtures in checks.test.mjs

samples.summary: The re-echo of mark-ready's log (`cat … || true`) is not pinned by the promote-step test
samples.evidence: mark-ready.test.mjs's `agent-review-panel.yml handles every mark-ready code, defaults the rest` asserts the redirect (`> "$RUNNER_TEMP/mark-ready.log" 2>&1`), the absence of a pipe, `code=$?`, the `case` branches and the outcome vocabulary — but nothing asserts the `cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/mark-ready.log" || true` that puts the gate report back into the step log. samples.summary: The rewritten hand-off comment's new claims are not asserted by any test
samples.evidence: The hand-off body now makes specific, load-bearing claims (based on the default branch, branch supplies no CI-defining path, and an explicit non-claim about weakened tests). The only assertion over the comment is `comment?.includes(HANDOFF_MARKER)` in `exit 0: --promote flips the PR, sets one lifecycle label, posts the hand-off`. If the claim text and the gates drift apart (e.g. gate 1b is weakened but the comment keeps asserting it), no test notices. Low impact — it is prose in a comment — hence nit.

finding.summary: The new `workflow_run.path` gate in agent-iterate-ci.yml has no test at all
finding.evidence: The diff adds `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` to the `gate` job of agent-iterate-ci.yml — the arm that drives a `contents: write` fixer. checks.test.mjs pins the equivalent clause only for agent-review-panel.yml (the gate/concurrency evaluator at checks.test.mjs:169-218 reads `^ {2}gate:` out of `agent-review-panel.yml` and nothing else). I grepped scripts/ for `workflow_run.path` (only checks.mjs and checks.test.mjs's panel test match) and for `agent-iterate-ci` (only loop-status.test.mjs's CI_PAGED_LATCH string test and comments in agent-workflow-guards.test.mjs). Deleting the new clause from agent-iterate-ci.yml leaves every suite green, so this guard can be regressed silently — the same class of silent-skip the change's own comments say must never happen.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing test exists. scripts/agent/checks.test.mjs:553-605 ("every workflow_run consumer CI can drive gates on the CI workflow's PATH") iterates over three workflow/job pairs — including ["agent-iterate-ci.yml", "gate"] at line 582 — reads the real file from .github/workflows, extracts the job's `if: >-` expression (line 589), substitutes every non-path sub-expression with a satisfying value (lines 569-578) so `path` is the only free variable, compiles it into a predicate, and asserts admits(CI_WORKFLOW_PATH) (line 593), !admits(".github/workflows/pwn.yml") (lines 594-597), and !admits for "", undefined and null (lines 601-603). Deleting the `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` clause at .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:54 makes the pwn.yml and absent-path assertions fail, since all other clauses are substituted true — so the guard cannot be regressed silently. The gate job's shape (lines 43-56) matches the extraction regex, the trigger is also pinned via `workflows: ["CI"]` (line 588), and the file runs under scripts/agent/package.json:8 (`node --test '**/*.test.mjs'`). The finding's premise that only agent-review-panel.yml is pinned is not true of this working tree.

finding.summary: The new `workflow_run.path` clause in ci-report.yml is untested; nothing pins the job's `if:`
finding.evidence: ci-report.yml's job `if:` is rewritten to add `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'`. scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs contains many ci-report.yml assertions (inline glob matcher, token scoping, step requires, GATE_STEP, comment interpolation) but none extract or evaluate the job's `if:` expression — I read the match list for `ci-report` across scripts/ and none of the hits touch the trigger gate. So the clause (and the `event == 'pull_request'` clause it now folds into a `>-` block) can be dropped or mis-edited with no failing test, on the one path the diff's own comment says fires on PR branches where forgery is not merge-gated.

verdict.reason: The claim that nothing pins ci-report.yml's job `if:` is false. scripts/agent/checks.test.mjs:553-605 ("every workflow_run consumer CI can drive gates on the CI workflow's PATH") explicitly includes ["ci-report.yml", "report"] (line 583), regex-extracts that job's `if: >-` block (line 589, with an assertion at line 590 that extraction succeeded), substitutes every non-path term with a satisfying value (lines 569-578, including workflow_run.event -> 'pull_request'), evaluates the expression, and asserts it admits CI_WORKFLOW_PATH (line 593), refuses '.github/workflows/pwn.yml' (lines 594-597), and refuses '', undefined and null (lines 601-603). It also pins `workflows: ["CI"]` (line 588) so the assertion stays aimed at the display-name trigger. Dropping or mis-editing the `path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` clause in .github/workflows/ci-report.yml:54-56 therefore fails this test, and deleting the `if:` block entirely fails the extraction assertion. The test file runs under the agent:tests lane (scripts/agent/package.json:8, glob '**/*.test.mjs'), whose per-file coverage is itself pinned by scripts/agent/eval/test-lane.test.mjs:113. The reviewer searched only scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs; the coverage lives beside the CI_WORKFLOW_PATH constant in scripts/agent/.

finding.summary: "the copies agree" test compares checks.mjs against a re-implementation inside the test, not against the workflow YAML
finding.evidence: checks.test.mjs:596-616 declares `const inline = (runs) => {...}` — a hand copy pasted into the test file — and then asserts `ciRunToRerun(fixture)` equals `inline(fixture)` for six fixtures. That loop can never fail because of anything in agent-loop.yml or agent-rerun.yml; it compares checks.mjs to the test's own copy. The only real link to the YAML is three regexes (`r\.status === 'completed'`, `r\.id > n\.id`, the `if (run) { await ... reRunWorkflow` shape) over a fixed `yml.slice(at - 200, at + 700)` window. Concretely: reverting the diff's `github.paginate(..., per_page: 100)` back to `listWorkflowRuns({... per_page: 1})` keeps every one of those regexes matching (the filter/reduce lines are unchanged) while restoring the exact defect the diff sets out to fix — with the newest run still in flight, `completed` is empty and `@claude rerun` re-runs nothing. The pagination/per_page part of the change is therefore unpinned while the test's title claims the copies are pinned.

verdict.reason: The test in this working tree does not match the finding's description on any of its three claims. (1) No hand copy exists: there is no "const inline = (runs) => {...}" anywhere in scripts/agent/checks.test.mjs — grep for "const inline" across scripts/agent returns only harvest.mjs:1990 and two unrelated eval tests. Lines 585-636, where the finding places the copy, are the workflow_run.path admittance test and the ci.yml trigger-race test. (2) The mirror is EXTRACTED FROM THE YAML AND EXECUTED, not re-typed: checks.test.mjs:768-770 matches the "const completed = ... const run = completed.reduce(...);" source out of the workflow text and builds new Function("all", src + "return run;"), then compares mirror(fixture) to ciRunToRerun(fixture) over seven fixtures (732-743, 772-778), with an anti-stub assertion at 781 requiring the extracted code to actually select a run. That regex matches the real YAML source (agent-loop.yml:159-160, agent-rerun.yml:203-204), so the loop CAN fail because of changes to those workflows — the opposite of the claim. (3) The pagination/per_page part is explicitly pinned: checks.test.mjs:760-762 asserts the block matches "github.paginate(github.rest.actions.listWorkflowRuns", asserts "per_page: 100" matches, and asserts "per_page: 1" does NOT appear. The finding's own concrete revert scenario (listWorkflowRuns with per_page: 1) would fail all three of those assertions, and a 101-run fixture at line 742 additionally targets the page-2 case. Also note the test window is yml.slice(at - 400, at + 700), not the quoted at - 200. The described defect is not present as described.

finding.summary: Gate 1b's pagination is never exercised — the stub cannot even express a second page, so a reader that only ever looks at page 1 passes the whole suite
finding.evidence: `branchEditsCiDefinition` (mark-ready.mjs:181-195) loops up to 10 pages, continues while `files.length === 100`, and throws (fail-closed) past 1000 files. The stub's files branch is `page === 1 ? cfg.files || [] : []` (mark-ready.test.mjs:79-83), and every fixture in the new gate-1b test (lines 269-298) supplies 1-item single pages, so `files.length < 100` returns on page 1 in every run. Nothing asserts that a workflow edit appearing only on page 2+ is caught, and nothing asserts the >1000-file `throw` reaches the fail-closed exit-1 path. Delete the loop and keep only page 1, or invert the `< 100` continuation, and all tests still pass — while an `agent:managed` PR with >100 changed files that guts `.github/workflows/ci.yml` would auto-promote on its own gutted CI run, which is exactly the attack gate 1b is advertised to close. Searched mark-ready.test.mjs for `page=`, `per_page`, `1000 changed files` (one hit, in the stub itself).

verdict.reason: A dedicated pagination test exists and the stub does express multiple pages, contrary to the finding. mark-ready.test.mjs:93-102 parses `page=N` from the URL and serves `cfg.filePages[page-1]` (single-page `files` is only a shorthand); the quoted stub snippet `page === 1 ? cfg.files || [] : []` is not in the file (79-83 is the repo-metadata branch). mark-ready.test.mjs:361-402 then exercises exactly the behaviors said to be unasserted: a `.github/workflows/ci.yml` edit sitting on PAGE 2 must exit 1 with the path named in stderr (367-373) — which a page-1-only reader would fail; a full first page followed by a short second page must still promote with exactly 2 file requests (377-385), which kills the inverted-`< 100` mutant; ten full pages must exit 1 with `/more than 1000 changed files/` (390-394), proving the throw at mark-ready.mjs:213 reaches the fail-closed catch at 262-269; and a non-array page must exit 1 with `/unexpected response from the PR files endpoint/` (398-401). The function is also named `ciDefiningPathsChanged` (mark-ready.mjs:193-214), not `branchEditsCiDefinition`, suggesting the finding describes a different revision.
